report.summary: The one failing test, test_current_year_is_accepted, is wrong: it creates a book with year=THIS_YEAR + 1 (next year) and expects 201, but the app deliberately rejects any year above the current year with 422. Fix the test to use THIS_YEAR (the current year), which is the boundary the test name describes; no application change is needed.

causes.title: Test submits next year and expects it to be accepted
causes.explanation: The test is named test_current_year_is_accepted, but it passes year=THIS_YEAR + 1. The app's validation only allows years from 1 up to the current year, so a next-year value is correctly refused with 422. The same file's parametrized test_invalid_book_is_rejected case 'next-year' asserts that exact rejection, so the two tests contradict each other and the app is behaving as intended. The fix is to use year=THIS_YEAR in the test so it checks the accepted boundary.
evidence: tests\api\test_books_api.py:47-50: def test_current_year_is_accepted(api): response = api.create_book(title=unique("New"), author="Someone", year=THIS_YEAR + 1); assert response.status_code == 201
app/main.py:82-84: this_year = date.today().year / if not 1 <= book.year <= this_year: / raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")
tests/api/test_books_api.py:58: ({"title": "T", "author": "A", "year": THIS_YEAR + 1}, "Year must be between"), expects 422 for next year
Failure output: assert 422 == 201 where 422 = <Response [422 Unprocessable Entity]>.status_code
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/api/test_books_api.py line 48, change year=THIS_YEAR + 1 to year=THIS_YEAR so the test checks that the current year is accepted. Leave the next-year rejection case in test_invalid_book_is_rejected as it is.
